brief: A spending tracker where categories are geological layers — deeper is necessity, surface is discretionary

dominant_strengths: Earth-strata color ramp from sand to bedrock is a perfect literal mapping of the geological metaphor to spending depth
Cross-section visualization reads instantly as both data and earth layers, creating strong conceptual payoff
Right-rail breakdown into Discretionary/Essential/Depth Ratio reinforces the metaphor with quantitative grounding
dominant_weaknesses: Left sidebar duplicates the central chart's information almost verbatim, wasting scarce real estate and weakening hierarchy
Typography is competent but generic sans — misses an opportunity for geological/scientific specimen-label character
Bar widths are uniform regardless of amount, so the chart encodes order but not magnitude — weakens behavioral utility
fix_priorities: Encode dollar amounts via bar height or width so the cross-section actually visualizes magnitude, not just sequence
Collapse or repurpose the redundant left sidebar — perhaps to time-series or drill-down per layer
Introduce a more characterful display face or specimen-label treatment for layer names to deepen the geological identity
Add subtle texture/grain to layers so they feel like sediment rather than flat color blocks
rationale.norman_balance: Strong visceral and reflective payoff from the metaphor, but behavioral utility lags because magnitudes aren't visually encoded.
rationale.intent_fit: Yes — the design literalizes the brief with genuine clarity, though it leans more illustrative than functional as a tracker.
